dealing_rules.basis: Same dealing arithmetic as the 90-Day Planner (assets/js/planner.js): long-form spreads across non-rest days by round-robin, shorts every other day; week 7 is the midpoint review.
rules: Long ideas are sorted by hook-strength score (highest first) before dealing — the best hooks earn the earliest weeks.
Longs deal round-robin across weeks: week 1 gets the top scores, not all of them at once.
Shorts and community ideas deal independently on their own cadence — they must never cannibalize a long slot.
Rest day is non-negotiable: no placement, analytics review only.
If ideas run out before slots, slots stay OPEN — never pad the calendar with filler. A visible gap is feedback: the bank needs ideas.
Surplus ideas stay in the bank as backlog — a full bank is a runway, not waste.
Week 7 (of 13) carries the midpoint review: kill the worst-performing format, double the best outlier.

batching.consistency_framing: Consistency beats volume — a cadence you can film is worth more than an ambitious one you abandon. The batching planner shows your film-day math honestly: if capacity doesn't cover cadence, shrink the cadence, don't promise yourself heroics.
guidance: Capacity = shoot_days_per_month × videos_per_shoot_day. Required = cadence × 52/12. Both are arithmetic on your own inputs.
A surplus means banked videos — publish steady, rest easy. A shortfall means a decision: add a shoot day, drop a slot, or merge formats.
Two short-form videos typically fit the effort of one long-form film block — budget shoot days by effort, not by count.
Never count 'I'll find the time' as capacity. Only scheduled, repeatable shoot days count.

repurposing_2_0.basis: Extends the wave-3 repurposing SOP (Phase 3, Everywhere Engine). The 2.0 map adds the full derivative map — every derivative must carry one original element (new hook, new framing, native caption). Repurposing is not re-uploading.

derivatives.effort: ~45 min each (edit for pacing, not re-upload)
derivatives.label: Short-form clip
derivatives.original_element: A fresh first 2 seconds — re-hook the clip, never reuse the pillar's intro
derivatives.task: Cut the best self-contained moment; burned-in captions, 9:16 reframe.

derivatives.label: Community reaction post
derivatives.original_element: A new question or poll written for the community tab — not the video title
derivatives.task: Post the debatable claim as a question or poll.

derivatives.label: TikTok cut
derivatives.task: Re-edit for TikTok pacing; keep 60–90s for Creator Rewards eligibility.
derivatives.original_element: Text-on-screen re-hook + native pacing — a re-edit, not a re-upload.

derivatives.label: Instagram Reel cut
derivatives.original_element: An aesthetic or save-worthy framing — transformation or reveal in the first 2 seconds
derivatives.task: Polished, save-worthy; caption as a mini-blog (5 hashtags).

derivatives.effort: ~1 hr (write the story around the numbers)
derivatives.label: Newsletter issue
derivatives.original_element: A written angle the video never states outright — the story behind the result
derivatives.task: Write the story around the video's numbers or result.

derivatives.label: X thread
derivatives.original_element: Written natively for X — first post is a new hook, not a link drop

derivatives.label: Facebook post
derivatives.task: Native upload of the best short as a Reel + discussion caption on your Page.
derivatives.original_element: A discussion-provoking caption ending with the debatable claim as a direct question.

repurposing_2_0.note: Cut 2–3 clips per pillar, not per platform — one clip per platform, each re-edited.

originality_guardrails.detail: The same video file uploaded to multiple platforms is distribution failure, not repurposing. Each derivative needs a native cut or a new hook.
A clip of the old intro dies on scroll. Every short-form derivative opens with a hook written for that platform.
originality_guardrails.rule: Every derivative gets a new hook

originality_guardrails.detail: Watermarks, letterboxed 16:9 on vertical, copy-pasted captions — platforms and viewers both punish it.
A community post that is just the video title is noise. Write the question the audience argues about.
originality_guardrails.rule: Text derivatives are written, not extracted

originality_guardrails.detail: If the pillar scores under 3/4 on the atom test (standalone hook, visual moment, quotable line, debatable claim), publish the pillar only — skip the repurposing and save the hours.
originality_guardrails.rule: Atom test gates the whole pipeline

deal_slots.description: Sponsored content slots reserved inside the content calendar. Pricing lives in the Deal Room and the 2026 rate card — the calendar only reserves the slots.
guidance: Reserve 1 slot per 4–6 organic pieces so sponsors never outnumber your own voice — an over-sponsored calendar bleeds trust.
Sponsor slots get the same hook-strength scoring as organic ideas; a weak sponsored video still costs you audience.
A sponsor slot is a calendar commitment, not a deal. Price it in the Deal Room (deal-room.html) before you promise it.
Links: the Deal Room (deal-room.html) for negotiation and the rate card (rate-card.html) for 2026 ranges.

simulator_bridge.description: Feed the calendar's cadence into the Empire Simulator as starting inputs. The simulator is a model, not a prediction.
